question: (93 + 14) − 56 × 2 + 33 + 15 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 43.

GIVEN

• (93 + 14) − 56 × 2 + 33 + 15

SOLUTION

• Apply BODMAS. Bracket: 93 + 14 = 107.

• Multiply: 56 × 2 = 112.

• 107 − 112 + 33 + 15 = −5 + 33 + 15 = 28 + 15 = 43.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Group the plus terms and minus terms separately: (107 + 33 + 15) − 112 = 155 − 112 = 43, avoiding sign errors.

NOTE

• BODMAS order: Brackets → Of → Division → Multiplication → Addition → Subtraction. Always finish × and ÷ before + and −.

question: 55 + 61 − 43 + (28 + 19) × 2 − 57 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 110.

GIVEN

• 55 + 61 − 43 + (28 + 19) × 2 − 57

SOLUTION

• Bracket: 28 + 19 = 47; then 47 × 2 = 94.

• 55 + 61 − 43 + 94 − 57 = 116 − 43 + 94 − 57.

• = 73 + 94 − 57 = 167 − 57 = 110.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Add all positives (55 + 61 + 94 = 210) and all negatives (43 + 57 = 100); 210 − 100 = 110.

NOTE

• Solve brackets and the multiplication first, then handle + and − left to right — a core BODMAS habit for SSC simplification.

question: 74 − 48 + 39 of 2 + 27 ÷ 3 − (18 × 1) + 16 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 111.

GIVEN

• 74 − 48 + 39 of 2 + 27 ÷ 3 − (18 × 1) + 16

SOLUTION

• 'Of' and division first: 39 of 2 = 78; 27 ÷ 3 = 9; 18 × 1 = 18.

• 74 − 48 + 78 + 9 − 18 + 16.

• = 26 + 78 + 9 − 18 + 16 = 113 − 18 + 16 = 111.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Positives: 74 + 78 + 9 + 16 = 177; negatives: 48 + 18 = 66; 177 − 66 = 111.

NOTE

• 'Of' ranks with multiplication and is done right after brackets — e.g. 39 of 2 means 39 × 2 = 78.

question: 76 + 41 − 24 + 38 ÷ 2 + (27 of 1) − 36 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 103.

GIVEN

• 76 + 41 − 24 + 38 ÷ 2 + (27 of 1) − 36

SOLUTION

• Division and 'of' first: 38 ÷ 2 = 19; 27 of 1 = 27.

• 76 + 41 − 24 + 19 + 27 − 36.

• = 117 − 24 + 19 + 27 − 36 = 93 + 19 + 27 − 36 = 139 − 36 = 103.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Positives: 76 + 41 + 19 + 27 = 163; negatives: 24 + 36 = 60; 163 − 60 = 103.

NOTE

• Resolve ÷ and 'of' before running the running total of + and − to prevent order mistakes.

question:
The pie chart given below shows the number of students studying in 5 sections of a class. The data is presented in the terms of degrees.

Total number of students studying in section C and D = 400.

Number of students studying in E are what percent of number of students studying in D?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 200%.

GIVEN

• Central angles: E = 24°, D = 12° (students are proportional to angles).

SOLUTION

• Required % = (E ÷ D) × 100 = (24 ÷ 12) × 100.

• = 2 × 100 = 200%.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• In a pie chart, students ∝ angle, so just compare the two angles: 24° is double 12°, hence 200%. No need to find actual counts.

NOTE

• Whole circle = 360° = total students. Any 'what percent of' between two sectors equals the ratio of their central angles × 100.

question:
The bar graph given below shows the number of pens sold by five given shops.

Which shop has sold maximum number of pens?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. D.

GIVEN

• Pens sold: A = 120, B = 150, C = 100, D = 180, E = 130.

SOLUTION

• Compare all bar heights: the tallest value is 180.

• Shop with 180 pens is D.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• For a 'maximum' bar question, just spot the tallest column visually — no arithmetic needed; here D clearly tops the graph.

NOTE

• In bar graphs the bar height directly equals the quantity, so highest bar = maximum and shortest bar = minimum.

question: A, B, and C can do a job in 12, 15, and 20 days, respectively. All three work together for 4 days. Then A leaves; B and C continue, but at only 3/4 of their normal daily hours. How many more days are needed to finish?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 2 2/7 days.

GIVEN

• A, B, C alone: 12, 15, 20 days. Total work (LCM) = 60 units.

SOLUTION

• Rates: A = 5, B = 4, C = 3 units/day.

• 3 together for 4 days = (5+4+3)×4 = 48 units; remaining = 60 − 48 = 12 units.

• B & C at 3/4 hours: rate = (4+3) × 3/4 = 21/4 units/day.

• Days = 12 ÷ (21/4) = 48/21 = 16/7 = 2 2/7 days.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Reducing hours to 3/4 simply multiplies B & C's efficiency by 3/4, so remaining time = normal time ÷ (3/4) = normal × 4/3. Remaining 12 units at 7/day = 12/7 days normally, ×4/3 = 16/7.

NOTE

• Take total work as LCM of the days; working at k fraction of hours multiplies daily output by k and divides the time needed by k.

question: In an election, there were only two candidates. One of the candidates secured 30% of the votes and was defeated by the other candidate by 3,65,104 votes. What is the total number of votes polled?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 912760.

GIVEN

• Loser got 30%, winner got 70%; margin of defeat = 3,65,104 votes.

SOLUTION

• Difference in vote share = 70% − 30% = 40% of total.

• 40% of total = 3,65,104 ⇒ total = 3,65,104 ÷ 0.40.

• Total = 912760 votes.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• With only two candidates, margin % = winner% − loser%. Here 40% → total = margin × 100/40 = 365104 × 5/2 = 912760.

NOTE

• In a two-candidate contest, if one gets x%, the other gets (100 − x)%; their difference (100 − 2x)% equals the winning margin.

question: A lender lends Rs. 10,000 at 8% per annum simple interest for t years and then lends an additional Rs. 5,000 at 12% per annum simple interest for the same period t. If the total simple interest at the end of t years is 5,400, find t (in years).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 3.86 years.

GIVEN

• Rs. 10,000 at 8% and Rs. 5,000 at 12%, both for t years; total SI = Rs. 5,400.

SOLUTION

• SI₁ = 10000 × 8 × t/100 = 800t; SI₂ = 5000 × 12 × t/100 = 600t.

• 800t + 600t = 1400t = 5400.

• t = 5400 ÷ 1400 = 27/7 ≈ 3.86 years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Combine the yearly interests first: 800 + 600 = Rs. 1400 per year. Then t = 5400 ÷ 1400 ≈ 3.86 directly.

NOTE

• Simple interest SI = P × R × T / 100. For several sums over the same period, add their per-year interests and divide the total interest by that sum.

question: A man borrowed Rs. 18,000 at 10% per annum simple interest. After 3 years, he repaid the borrowed money along with the interest by giving a motorcycle worth 12,000 and the remaining in cash. Find the amount of cash he paid.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. Rs.11,400.

GIVEN

• Principal = Rs. 18,000, Rate = 10% p.a. SI, Time = 3 years; motorcycle worth Rs. 12,000 given.

SOLUTION

• SI = 18000 × 10 × 3 / 100 = Rs. 5,400.

• Total repayable = 18000 + 5400 = Rs. 23,400.

• Cash = 23400 − 12000 = Rs.11,400.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• 10% for 3 years = 30% of 18,000 = 5,400 interest. Amount 23,400 minus the 12,000 bike = 11,400 cash.

NOTE

• Amount = Principal + SI. When part of a repayment is made in kind (goods), subtract the goods' value from the total amount to get the cash portion.

question: Manju sold a scooty with a tagged price of Rs.1,25,000. After applying a trade concession, the final transaction value became Rs.70,000. Calculate the percentage discount given on the marked price.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 44%.

GIVEN

• Marked (tagged) price = Rs. 1,25,000; selling (final) price = Rs. 70,000.

SOLUTION

• Discount amount = 1,25,000 − 70,000 = Rs. 55,000.

• Discount % = (55,000 ÷ 1,25,000) × 100.

• = 44 = 44%.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Discount % = (1 − SP/MP) × 100 = (1 − 70/125) × 100 = (55/125) × 100 = 44%.

NOTE

• Discount is always reckoned on the Marked Price: Discount% = (MP − SP)/MP × 100.

question: A trader buys an article at Rs.3,500 and marks it up by 35%. He gives two successive discounts of 20% and 10%. What is his net profit or loss percentage?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. Loss of 2.8%.

GIVEN

• CP = Rs. 3,500; mark-up 35%; successive discounts 20% and 10%.

SOLUTION

• MP = 3500 × 1.35 = Rs. 4,725.

• After discounts: 4725 × 0.80 × 0.90 = 4725 × 0.72 = Rs. 3,402 = SP.

• SP < CP, loss = 3500 − 3402 = 98; Loss% = 98/3500 × 100 = 2.8%.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Net factor = 1.35 × 0.8 × 0.9 = 0.972 of CP. Since 0.972 < 1, it is a loss of (1 − 0.972) = 0.028 = 2.8%.

NOTE

• Chain the multipliers: SP = CP × (1+markup) × (1−d₁) × (1−d₂). A final factor below 1 means loss, above 1 means profit.

question: Two cars start from the same point at the same time, moving in the same direction. The first car travels at 60 km/h, and the second car at 90 km/h. After how much time will they be 45 km apart?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 1 hour 30 minutes.

GIVEN

• Same direction speeds 60 km/h and 90 km/h; required gap = 45 km.

SOLUTION

• Relative speed (same direction) = 90 − 60 = 30 km/h.

• Time = distance ÷ relative speed = 45 ÷ 30 = 1.5 h.

• 1.5 h = 1 hour 30 minutes.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Gap grows at (90 − 60) = 30 km every hour, so 45 km gap takes 45/30 = 1½ hours.

NOTE

• Same direction ⇒ subtract speeds; opposite directions ⇒ add speeds. Time to reach a given separation = separation ÷ relative speed.

question: Two cyclists start at the same time from towns A and B, which are 210 km apart, and travel towards each other. The cyclist from A rides at 28 km/h, and the cyclist from B rides at 32 km/h. Find the time (in hours) taken by the cyclist from B to reach town A after meeting.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 3.06 hours.

GIVEN

• Distance AB = 210 km; A at 28 km/h, B at 32 km/h, moving towards each other.

SOLUTION

• Meeting time = 210 ÷ (28 + 32) = 210 ÷ 60 = 3.5 h.

• Distance A covered = 28 × 3.5 = 98 km = distance B must still cover to reach A.

• Time for B = 98 ÷ 32 = 3.0625 ≈ 3.06 hours.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• After meeting, B's remaining distance to A equals A's speed × meeting time = 28 × 3.5 = 98 km; divide by B's speed 32 → ≈3.06 h.

NOTE

• When two bodies move towards each other, meeting time = total distance ÷ sum of speeds; the distance each covers is its own speed × that time.

question: Two cyclists start from two towns, A and B, which are 180 km apart, and move towards each other. The cyclist from A rides at 40 km/h, while the cyclist from B rides at 50 km/h. However, the cyclist from A starts 45 minutes earlier. Find the time (in hours, rounded to two decimals) after A's start when they meet.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 2.42 h.

GIVEN

• AB = 180 km; A at 40 km/h starts 45 min (0.75 h) before B at 50 km/h; towards each other.

SOLUTION

• In the 0.75 h head start, A covers 40 × 0.75 = 30 km; remaining gap = 180 − 30 = 150 km.

• Closing speed after B starts = 40 + 50 = 90 km/h; time = 150 ÷ 90 = 1.667 h.

• Total after A's start = 0.75 + 1.667 = 2.4167 ≈ 2.42 h.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Subtract the head-start distance (30 km) from 180, then divide the rest by combined speed and add back the 0.75 h: 150/90 + 0.75 = 2.42 h.

NOTE

• For a head start, first reduce the gap by the early distance, then use meeting time = remaining gap ÷ sum of speeds, and add the head-start time to the answer.

question:
In the given figure, angle BCD = 155 degrees and angle ABC = 85 degrees. What is the value (in degrees) of angle BAC?

[Figure: triangle ABC with side AC extended beyond C to point D; angle BCD is the exterior angle at C.]
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 70.

GIVEN

• In triangle ABC, AC is extended to D; exterior angle BCD = 155°, angle ABC = 85°.

SOLUTION

• Exterior angle = sum of the two remote interior angles.

• angle BCD = angle BAC + angle ABC ⇒ 155 = angle BAC + 85.

• angle BAC = 155 − 85 = 70°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Just subtract the given interior angle from the exterior angle: 155 − 85 = 70°, no need to find the third angle.

NOTE

• Exterior Angle Theorem: an exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two non-adjacent (remote) interior angles.

question:
In the given figure, angle PSQ = 125 degrees and angle PRT = 110 degrees. What is the value (in degrees) of angle SPR?

[Figure: P is the apex; Q, S, R, T lie on a straight line with PS and PR drawn to it. angle PSQ and angle PRT are exterior angles of triangle PSR at S and R.]
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 55.

GIVEN

• Straight line Q–S–R–T; angle PSQ = 125°, angle PRT = 110°.

SOLUTION

• Linear pairs: angle PSR = 180 − 125 = 55°; angle PRS = 180 − 110 = 70°.

• In triangle PSR: angle SPR = 180 − (55 + 70).

• = 180 − 125 = 55°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• angle SPR = (angle PSQ + angle PRT) − 180 = (125 + 110) − 180 = 55°, using both exterior angles at once.

NOTE

• Angles on a straight line sum to 180° (linear pair) and the three interior angles of a triangle sum to 180°.
